title: Direct Knowledge Of Allah 19th Degree 1st Truth From Searching In Absentia To Direct Address

questions.question: What big truth does the traveller learn from the universe in this passage?
questions.answer: He learns that all creation points to Allah as the only true God and shows His oneness.

questions.question: How is the universe described to help us understand its meaning?
questions.answer: It is described like a great book, a grand palace, and a well-ordered city.

questions.question: What does calling all other things “contingent” mean here?
questions.answer: It means everything besides Allah depends on Him and does not exist by itself.

questions.question: What kinds of parts of the universe are said to agree together in giving testimony?
questions.answer: Its foundations, kinds, pieces, tiny parts, living things, contents, and all that comes in and goes out.

questions.question: Which three ideas about the world are mentioned as signs that point to Allah?
questions.answer: Its being created, its constant changing, and its dependent nature.

questions.question: What group of learned people is mentioned as supporting this truth?
questions.answer: The scholars of Islamic theology.

questions.question: What does the traveller do after learning through many levels?
questions.answer: He comes near to a higher level of faith and begins speaking directly to Allah.

questions.question: Why does the traveller speak to his own soul?
questions.answer: He is reminding himself to turn from only indirect searching to directly addressing Allah.

questions.question: What change happens when the word meaning “You alone” is reached in the opening sura?
questions.answer: The speech changes from talking about Allah to speaking directly to Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say we should stop doing?
questions.answer: We should stop only searching in an indirect way.

questions.question: From whom should the seeker ask about the One he is looking for?
questions.answer: He should ask the One he is seeking.

questions.question: What example is given with the sun?
questions.answer: Since the sun shows other things, it can also show itself even more clearly.

questions.question: How can people try to know their Creator?
questions.answer: They can try to know Him through His Beautiful Names and Holy Attributes, as much as they are able.

questions.question: Who is the main human figure in the passage?
questions.answer: A passionate and curious traveller looking for the Creator.

questions.question: What had this traveller already gained before this moment?
questions.answer: He had gained indirect knowledge of Allah through eighteen stages.

questions.question: Where had he spiritually arrived by the end of that journey?
questions.answer: He had reached a high level of belief near the throne of truth.

questions.question: What new way of speaking begins at that point?
questions.answer: He begins to address Allah directly.

questions.question: What part of the opening sura is described as praise said in an indirect way?
questions.answer: The part from the beginning until the word that means “You alone.”

questions.question: What does that special word show?
questions.answer: It shows entering into Allah’s presence and speaking to Him directly.

questions.question: What lesson does the traveller take from that change in wording?
questions.answer: He learns that he should turn from indirect seeking to direct asking.

questions.question: Why is direct asking better in the example given?
questions.answer: Because the one who makes things known can make itself known even more clearly.

questions.question: How does the sun example help explain this lesson?
questions.answer: We know the sun by its rays, so in a similar way we can know our Creator by His signs.

questions.question: What two ways of knowing Allah are named at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: Through His Most Beautiful Names and His Sacred Attributes.

questions.question: Does the passage teach that people can fully know Allah on their own without limits?
questions.answer: No. It says we know Him according to our capacity.

questions.question: What is the shortest statement of belief taught in the first paragraph?
questions.answer: Allah alone is God, and He has no equal.

questions.question: What does the passage say about anything besides Allah?
questions.answer: Everything else is dependent and not necessary by itself.

questions.question: Name one picture used for the universe in the passage.
questions.answer: It is pictured as a great written book.

questions.question: Name another picture used for the universe in the passage.
questions.answer: It is also pictured as a beautiful palace.

questions.question: What do these pictures of the universe help the reader understand?
questions.answer: They help the reader understand that the universe has order, meaning, and a Maker.

questions.question: Why are change and renewal in the world important in this passage?
questions.answer: They are signs that the world is managed on purpose and is not independent.

questions.question: What is meant by the mention of things entering and leaving the universe?
questions.answer: It points to ongoing movement and control within creation.

questions.question: After these signs are mentioned, what does the traveller do?
questions.answer: He turns to direct speech with Allah.

questions.question: Why is the word meaning “You alone” so important here?
questions.answer: It marks the shift from speaking about Allah to speaking to Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say one should ask instead of only searching from far away?
questions.answer: One should ask the One being sought.

questions.question: According to the sun example, how do signs help us?
questions.answer: They guide us to know the source they come from.

questions.question: What are believers encouraged to use when trying to know Allah?
questions.answer: They are encouraged to reflect on His Names and Attributes.

questions.question: What does the passage say the cosmos points to?
questions.answer: It points to the necessary existence and oneness of Allah.

questions.question: Why is the universe compared to a city and a palace?
questions.answer: Because it is arranged, full of parts, and run in an orderly way.

questions.question: What do the many parts of the universe do together in this passage?
questions.answer: They all give a united witness to Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say can be clearly observed among beings?
questions.answer: Their cooperation, answering one another, supporting one another, balance, and protection.

questions.question: What can we understand from the world’s regular changes?
questions.answer: We can understand that it is under wise control, not random.

questions.question: How had the traveller mostly known Allah before this point?
questions.answer: He had known Allah indirectly through what he learned from creation.

questions.question: What caused the traveller to move to direct speech?
questions.answer: His climb in faith brought him to a nearness where he addressed Allah Himself.

questions.question: What lesson from Surah al-Fatihah is used in the passage?
questions.answer: The lesson that the words change from praise about Allah to speaking directly to Him.

questions.question: What should replace indirect searching, according to the traveller?
questions.answer: Directly asking Allah should replace it.

questions.question: What does the sun teach in this comparison?
questions.answer: The source of light can be known through the light it gives.

questions.question: How is knowing Allah similar to knowing the sun in this example?
questions.answer: Just as the sun is recognized by its rays, Allah is known through His Names and Attributes.

questions.question: What limit does the passage place on human understanding?
questions.answer: People can only know Allah as much as their ability allows.

questions.question: In this passage, what is the traveller searching for?
questions.answer: He is searching for the Creator of the world.

questions.question: What had he used to learn before speaking directly?
questions.answer: He had learned by looking at signs and proofs in creation.

questions.question: How many stages of indirect learning are mentioned?
questions.answer: Eighteen stages are mentioned.

questions.question: What kind of spiritual progress did he make through those stages?
questions.answer: He rose in faith and came to a higher station of belief.

questions.question: What does the traveller then say to his inner self?
questions.answer: He tells himself to leave indirect seeking and turn to direct asking.

questions.question: How is the earlier part of the opening sura described?
questions.answer: It is described as praise said without direct address.

questions.question: What does the word meaning “You alone” change in the style of speaking?
questions.answer: It changes the speech into direct address to Allah.

questions.question: Why is this change important for the traveller?
questions.answer: It teaches him that nearness to Allah should lead to speaking to Him directly.

questions.question: What example from nature is used to explain this idea?
questions.answer: The example of the sun and its rays is used.

questions.question: What do the rays help us know?
questions.answer: They help us recognize the sun.

questions.question: In the same way, what helps us know Allah?
questions.answer: His Beautiful Names and Sacred Attributes help us know Him.

questions.question: Does the passage teach that Allah has anything like Him?
questions.answer: No. It teaches that no equal to Him can exist.

questions.question: What belief sentence stands at the heart of this passage?
questions.answer: That there is no god but Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s uniqueness?
questions.answer: It teaches that nothing can be truly like Him.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the rest of creation compared with Allah?
questions.answer: The rest of creation is dependent and needs Him.

questions.question: How does the passage present the universe as something meaningful?
questions.answer: It presents it like a written message, a planned building, and an organized place.

questions.question: What does the agreement of so many parts of the universe suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests one wise Creator and one united plan.

questions.question: What truths about the world are named as part of its testimony?
questions.answer: Its being made, its changing, and its dependence.

questions.question: What other features among beings are named as signs?
questions.answer: Working together, responding to one another, helping one another, balance, and preservation.

questions.question: What happened after he learned through many stages?
questions.answer: He came to a point where he addressed Allah directly.

questions.question: What lesson is drawn from the opening chapter of the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The lesson is that a servant can move from praising Allah to speaking directly to Him.

questions.question: What practical step does the traveller say “we” should take?
questions.answer: We should leave behind only indirect searching and ask Allah directly.

questions.question: Why is the sun a helpful example in the passage?
questions.answer: Because it shows how a source can be known through what comes from it.

questions.question: Through what two things are people told to seek knowledge of their Creator?
questions.answer: Through His Most Beautiful Names and His Sacred Attributes.
